new_statements.quote: Slide 'S. Bauchi languages: tones' (video t=644 s, slide 14 of 21 in the saved transcript; verified on the frame image): "SB languages have either three tone (H/M/L) or two (H/[L; two characters hidden by the speaker inset]) plus downstep. Some languages have glide tones (falling / rising), but elsewhere they seem to be largely absent. Provisional prediction is that PSB had three tone levels (like much of neighbouring A3 for example) but is in the process of reducing in some languages". Tala itself appears only as a leaf of the slide 'South Bauchi languages family tree (provisonal)' (t=478 s, slide 9): "Lungu = Tala" (grouped next to Soor and Sho [=Ju]). No slide in the deck contains the words stress or accent.

new_statements.relation_note: new: nothing on record (no catalog record, no stress statement held by the project for tala1295). What the work adds is a FAMILY-LEVEL tone typology (2-3 level tones + downstep) for the South Bauchi group with Tala shown as a member ('Lungu = Tala' in the tree); it makes no word-stress statement and no Tala-specific prosodic statement, so it neither places stress nor denies it. Consistent with the tone-marked 'Lungu (Tala)' column of Shimizu 1978 already noted in this folder's.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Group-level statement only: the South Bauchi (West Chadic B3) languages, among which Blench's tree lists 'Lungu = Tala', are tone languages with either three (H/M/L) or two level tones plus downstep, contour tones in some languages; Proto-South-Bauchi provisionally reconstructed with three levels. Nothing is said about word stress or accent, for Tala or for the group, and nothing Tala-specific is said about tone.
new_statements.exceptions: none (the only per-language prosodic remarks concern Zul and Zaar: pronoun number and Zaar perfective/imperfective marked by tone)
new_statements.identity_note: Blench treats the language under the label 'Lungu = Tala' as one leaf of his provisional South Bauchi tree (next to Soor and Sho [=Ju]); the prosodic (tone) statement is made for the South Bauchi group as a whole, not for Tala or any Tala dialect specifically.

sources.note: No prose on tone or stress anywhere on the page (0 occurrences of tone/stress/accent outside the gloss 'stone'). The Lungu (Tala) column is complete (108 forms) with impressionistic tone diacritics on 79 vowels (acute, grave, circumflex; many syllables unmarked), e.g. arm aa, ash kiîsi, bark kwoplaŋ, belly kaado, bird yaasi, blood prà, bone kuul, breast nyii, fire wudî, heart/liver mbasí, moon lii, one nóm, two pàp, tongue ndéláŋ, tooth shín, water maal. Shows Shimizu transcribed Tala with H, L and falling marks; no stress marks; no analysis.
